conviction_note: Q3 numbers are not pre-released and the dividend is a live decision, so the move is sized as a new-numbers print (5.0%), but there is no sourced consensus and every factual item (33 Atlantic off-hire days in Q3, the USD 37m tax refund, the contract news, the broker target raises) is already public. p_up sits at 51, so the scaled number is +0.1. The findings sum to 0.0: small positives on dividend capacity and possible insurance income are cancelled by the bar having risen into the print.

already_public.what: Deepsea Atlantic back on rate 2 Aug after 106 off-hire days, 73 of them in Q2, so about 33 fall in Q3

Q2 report: underlying EBITDA USD 129m, dividend held at USD 0.25, leverage 1.5x, incident net cash impact about USD -35m of which USD 7m in Q2 and the rest 'spread across the coming quarters', insurance claim above USD 82.5m held as a contingent asset
Tax case final: about USD 37m (NOK 307m plus interest and costs) to be repaid to ODL; the upfront payment was already carried as a receivable
Vår Energi LOA for Deepsea Bergen, USD 518m, 2028-2031
Equinor exercises two more wells on Deepsea Atlantic, firm to late Q4 2027
Beacon Pacific management agreement (Serica, UK, from Q3 2027)
Broker target raises into the print: Fearnley upgrades to buy, TP 120 (106), 20 Oct; SEB TP 120 (114), 21 Oct; ABG TP 120 (110), 2 Nov

new_in_release.expect: Q3 EBITDA with the Atlantic down about 33 days; there is no sourced consensus. Arithmetic on Q1 (154) and underlying Q2 (129) gives roughly the high 140s, but the bar is unknown
Q3 dividend. The 0.25 was held in Q2; the record is 0.18, 0.20, 0.23, 0.25, 0.25, and the tax refund and lower leverage leave room for a raise. A modest lean up
whether the contingent insurance asset is recognised as Q3 other income (a one-off, up), and the remaining incident cash drag (guided, down)
tax refund timing and net debt; likely down from 863, direction of surprise unknown
ODL gives no formal numeric guide; possible commentary on the Nordkapp 2028 rate (due by end-2026) and Atlantic availability from late 2027; unknown

bar: unsourced: no published Q3 2026 consensus was found (the company IR page lists 8 covering analysts and no consensus, and searches of the Norwegian and English press turned up nothing), so every finding is capped small. Reference: https://www.odfjelldrilling.com/investor/analyst-coverage/

The issuer's own notice of 27 Oct says the Q3 earnings announcement is on Tuesday 3 November with a webcast at 14:00 CET the same day (https://api3.oslo.oslobors.no/v1/newsreader/message?messageId=684889). ODL's Q2 report was stamped 05:00 UTC on NewsWeb (https://api3.oslo.oslobors.no/v1/newsreader/message?messageId=680025), and the MFN calendar lists the Q3 report at 07:05 CET, before the 09:00 Oslo open.
positioning_check: No disclosed net short position at or above 0.5% in the Finanstilsynet SSR register as of 2026-10-30 (https://ssr.finanstilsynet.no/api/v2/instruments). anchor_covered is false, so this is the truncation floor and not evidence that nobody is short; the change is 0.0 on the register. The lean is run-up only (-0.545); run-up is +10.9% over 20 days and +23.1% over 60.

findings.finding: The Supreme Court refused the tax appeal on 2 Sep, so about USD 37m comes back to ODL. With leverage down to 1.5x and a record of raising the dividend (0.18, 0.20, 0.23, 0.25, then held at 0.25 through the Atlantic incident), that gives the board room to lift the Q3 dividend or add a special.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025, dividend raised 0.18 to 0.20: 0.0%. Q4 2025, raised to 0.23: +4.7%. Q1 2026, raised to 0.25: -1.24%. Q2 2026, held at 0.25 after the incident: +3.8%. Mixed.
findings.why_not_priced: The refund itself is public and modelled. The decision on what the board does with it is not. If a raise were fully priced, the brokers' November notes would quote a specific dividend; none was found, and only the retail forum talks about 'skru opp utbytte'.
findings.independence: Dividend history and leverage from the Q2 presentation: https://api3.oslo.oslobors.no/v1/newsreader/attachment?messageId=680025&attachmentId=331296

findings.finding: The Q2 presentation said the Atlantic incident has a net cash impact of about USD 35m, of which USD 7m was in Q2 and 'the remainder expected to be spread across the coming quarters'. On top of about 33 off-hire days in Q3, that is a guided drag on Q3 cash flow and possibly on EBITDA.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 was the incident quarter, with the headline flattered by insurance income; the stock rose 3.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it lands inside what the company guided, so it is near zero. The only unpriced part is the quarterly phasing, and the release will show it.

findings.finding: At Q2 the insurance claim above the recognised USD 82.5m was treated as a contingent asset. If any of it is recognised in Q3 it would show as other income, a one-off lift to EBITDA.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 recognised USD 82m of insurance (+USD 32m net EBITDA); the stock rose 3.8%, but the market was told the underlying figure was 129.
findings.why_not_priced: The timing of recognition is not disclosed. It is a one-off with no path to the run-rate, so it is sized at a fraction of the cash; the market looked through the last one by quoting underlying EBITDA.

findings.finding: The bar has moved up into the print. Fearnley upgraded to buy (TP 120 from 106) on 20 Oct, SEB raised to TP 120 (114) on 21 Oct, and ABG raised to TP 120 (110) on the morning of 2 Nov, while the stock rose 10.9% in 20 days to about NOK 109.4. The Nordnet retail thread is talking about quarterly EBITDA 'rett sør for musd 200' and sharp dividend raises.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025, after a strong run: 0.0%. Q1 2024: -6.19%. The history does not separate run-up days cleanly.
findings.original_quote: ABG Sundal Collier höjer riktkursen för Odfjell Drilling till 120 norska kronor (110), upprepar köp; Fearnley höjer Odfjell Drilling till köp (behåll), riktkurs 120 norska kronor (106); forum: 'så snakker en vel fort rett sør for musd 200 EBITDA i kvartalet??'
findings.why_not_priced: It is partly the price itself. The point is that the expectation a print has to clear is now higher than the 129 underlying Q2 base. Arithmetic on Q1 (154) and Q2 (129 plus about 33 off-hire days recovered) gives the high 140s, well short of the retail 200 talk. If the market held realistic expectations, the run-up and target raises would not have arrived in the last two weeks before a print with no new contract of size.

findings.finding: On 2 Nov ODL announced a management agreement for the 6G semi Beacon Pacific (Serica, UK, six firm wells from Q3 2027), taking the managed fleet to nine rigs. It adds external-fleet fees and mobilisation work; the stock moved +0.4% on the day.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced the day before. The release and call may quantify fees and reactivation scope, which the press release did not. External-fleet EBITDA is small next to the owned fleet's, so the effect is net small.

outside_window.finding: Deepsea Nordkapp's 2028 extension rate is to be set by two independent brokers by end-2026; if it is not in the Q3 release it lands after the window

baseline_tension: The findings net to zero against a -0.5 run-up lean, so they neither confirm nor contradict it. The one directional item, the bar rising on broker upgrades and the run-up, agrees with the lean, so it is sized small.
language_note: The Nordnet Norwegian retail thread shows inflated local expectations ('rett sør for musd 200 EBITDA', 'skru opp utbytte kraftig') that no English source carried.
The Nordic flash headlines on Nordnet gave the dated broker target raises (ABG 2 Nov, SEB 21 Oct, Fearnley 20 Oct), which the English searches returned only as stale May targets.
Every filing is English-only: ODL is Bermuda-domiciled and Aberdeen-run, so NewsWeb adds nothing in Norwegian.
lessons_applied: 'Right about the number, too small about the move': the Q3 numbers are new, not pre-released, so abs_move goes from 4.5 to 5.0 rather than staying anchored on the name's 3.6-3.8 history (held below Europe's 7.4% because there is no guide and the fleet is contracted).
'A beat made of a one-off is sold': the insurance contingent-asset finding is cut from +0.2 to +0.1.
'Finding inside guidance toward 0': the guided incident cash drag is cut from -0.2 to -0.1.
'A verified fact is not a predicted reaction': the dividend/tax-refund finding is cut from +0.4 to +0.3, and p_up from 52 to 51.
